Environmental Boxplots

Source: R/plotting.R
boxplot.Rd

Creates boxplots for environmental monitoring data. Boxplots are generated separately for each analyte and display the distribution of analytical results across sampling locations.

Usage

boxplot(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
boxplot(
  df,
  location,
  analyte,
  result,
  sample_date = NULL,
  reporting_flag = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
boxplot(
  df,
  coef = 1.5,
  scale_y_trans = "identity",
  show_points = FALSE,
  fill = NULL,
  notch = FALSE,
  plot_ci = FALSE,
  standards = FALSE,
  pnt = 2,
  short_name = FALSE,
  coord_flip = FALSE,
  legend_title = NULL,
  add_explanation = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location

Location column.

analyte

Analyte column.

result

Analytical result column.

sample_date

Sample date column.

reporting_flag

Reporting qualifier column.

unit

Reporting unit column.

coef

Length of whiskers expressed as a multiple of the interquartile range.

scale_y_trans

Transformation applied to the y-axis.

show_points

Logical. If `TRUE`, individual observations are displayed using either a beeswarm or jittered scatter overlay.

fill

Optional column name used to group and color boxplots. Must be supplied as a character string naming a column in `x`.

notch

Logical. If `TRUE`, notched boxplots are produced.

plot_ci

Logical. If `TRUE`, bootstrap confidence intervals for the mean are displayed.

standards

Logical. If `TRUE`, applicable standards are displayed on the plot.

pnt

Point size used for observations and summaries.

short_name

Logical. If `TRUE`, titles use `short_analyte_label()` values when available; otherwise `analyte_label()` values are used.

coord_flip

Logical. If `TRUE`, axes are flipped.

legend_title

Optional legend title.

add_explanation

Logical. If `TRUE`, an explanatory panel describing boxplot components is added.

Value

A named list of plots, with one plot generated for each analyte. List names correspond to the analyte values in the mapped analyte column.

A named list of plot objects. One boxplot is produced for each analyte in the mapped analyte column.

Details

The function is implemented as an S3 generic and supports both raw data frames and `env_schema` objects.

For data frames, `boxplot()` first converts the input data to an `env_schema` object using the supplied column mappings and then dispatches to [boxplot.env_schema()].

Schema-aware plotting

`boxplot()` is schema-aware and relies on accessor functions rather than hard-coded column names. Users are encouraged to convert raw environmental datasets to `env_schema` objects prior to analysis and visualization.

env_schema Method

Analyte grouping is determined by the mapped analyte variable, not by internal standardized analyte metadata columns.

For `env_schema` objects, `boxplot()` automatically uses the schema mappings and standardized analytical fields:

  • the mapped location field

  • the mapped analyte field

  • the mapped result field

  • the mapped reporting flag field

  • `analysis_unit()` for axis labeling

  • `analyte_label()` and `short_analyte_label()` for titles

This allows boxplots to be generated consistently regardless of the original source column names used by the underlying dataset.

Examples

data(gw)

plots <- boxplot(gw)

names(plots)

plots <- boxplot(
  gw_data,
  location = location_id,
  analyte = param_name,
  result = analysis_result
)
